info.title: Spring Boot Maven JPA project setup

diffs.patch:
Index: pom.xml
===================================================================
--- pom.xml	
+++ pom.xml	
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
+<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
+         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
+         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
+    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>
+
+    <parent>
+        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
+        <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
+        <version>3.5.3</version>
+        <relativePath/>
+    </parent>
+
+    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
+    <artifactId>demo</artifactId>
+    <version>0.0.1-SNAPSHOT</version>
+    <name>demo</name>
+    <description>Spring Boot service persisting data via JPA/Hibernate repositories</description>
+
+    <properties>
+        <java.version>21</java.version>
+    </properties>
+
+    <dependencies>
+        <dependency>
+            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
+            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
+        </dependency>
+
+        <dependency>
+            <groupId>com.h2database</groupId>
+            <artifactId>h2</artifactId>
+            <scope>runtime</scope>
+        </dependency>
+
+        <dependency>
+            <groupId>org.postgresql</groupId>
+            <artifactId>postgresql</artifactId>
+            <scope>runtime</scope>
+        </dependency>
+
+        <dependency>
+            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
+            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
+            <scope>test</scope>
+        </dependency>
+    </dependencies>
+
+    <build>
+        <plugins>
+            <plugin>
+                <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
+                <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
+            </plugin>
+        </plugins>
+    </build>
+
+</project>

Index: src/main/resources/application.properties
===================================================================
--- src/main/resources/application.properties	
+++ src/main/resources/application.properties	
@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+# Default profile uses a file-based H2 database so data persists across restarts.
+spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:file:./data/demo;DB_CLOSE_ON_EXIT=FALSE
+spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
+spring.datasource.username=sa
+spring.datasource.password=
+
+# Hibernate / JPA
+spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
+spring.jpa.open-in-view=false
+spring.jpa.show-sql=true
+spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.format_sql=true
+
+# H2 web console available at http://localhost:8080/h2-console
+spring.h2.console.enabled=true
+spring.h2.console.path=/h2-console
+
+# To use PostgreSQL instead, activate the "postgres" profile (see application-postgres.properties).

parts.text:
The .opencode directory is just opencode's own tooling. The repo is essentially empty. I need to scaffold a Maven Spring Boot project with JPA/Hibernate. Java/Maven aren't installed, so I can't run it, but I can create the project.

Let me plan the structure. A typical Maven Spring Boot project:

```
pom.xml
src/main/java/com/example/demo/DemoApplication.java
src/main/java/com/example/demo/domain/Customer.java (entity)
src/main/java/com/example/demo/repository/CustomerRepository.java
src/main/resources/application.properties
src/test/java/com/example/demo/...
.gitignore
```

The user says "using JPA/Hibernate repositories". I should include:
- Spring Boot Starter Data JPA (brings Hibernate)
- A relational DB driver — H2 for local dev (runtime), maybe PostgreSQL for prod. I'll use H2 for simplicity with a file-based DB so it truly persists. Actually keep it simple: H2 in-memory by default is not persistent. The user wants to "persist data to a relational database". I'll configure H2 file-based so persistence works, and mention switching to PostgreSQL/MySQL.

Let me pick a recent stable Spring Boot version. Today's date is 2026... but my knowledge. Let me check what versions are available. I can't access network reliably? Let me try webfetch maven central to get latest Spring Boot version. Actually let me just use a known stable version like 3.3.x or 3.4.x. Given date 2026, likely 3.5.x / 4.0.x. Better to check Maven Central.

Let me try fetching from search.maven.org. But maybe no network. Let me test.

Actually, let me first decide on group/artifact. Use com.example, artifact "demo", package com.example.demo. Or more meaningful: groupId com.example, artifactId inventory? The user didn't specify. I'll use `com.example` / `demo-service`? Keep neutral: artifactId `demo`, package `com.example.demo`.

Let me check network for latest version.
Empty output. Maybe no network. Let me try webfetch.

Latest is 3.5.3. I'll use that. Java version for Spring Boot 3.5 is Java 17+ (baseline 17, supports up to 24). I'll use Java 21 (LTS).

Now let me create the project. Use `start.spring.io` generated structure manually since no maven. Let me create a todo list since this is multi-step.

Files:
1. pom.xml
2. src/main/java/com/example/demo/DemoApplication.java
3. src/main/java/com/example/demo/domain/Customer.java
4. src/main/java/com/example/demo/repository/CustomerRepository.java
5. src/main/resources/application.properties
6. src/test/java/com/example/demo/repository/CustomerRepositoryTest.java
7. .gitignore
8. README.md? User didn't ask. Don't create docs proactively. But a brief README is common for project setup. Instructions say don't create documentation unless requested. Skip README.

Also maybe a CommandLineRunner demonstrating persistence, and a service. Keep it reasonable. The user asked to "set up a new Maven Spring Boot Java project that needs to persist data to a relational database using JPA/Hibernate repositories." So core deliverable: project skeleton + JPA entity + repository + config + test.

Let me include:
- Entity `Customer` with id, name, email, createdAt.
- Repository `CustomerRepository extends JpaRepository<Customer, Long>` with a derived query method.
- application.properties with datasource config.
- Use H2 file-based for dev so data persists, plus PostgreSQL profile? Keep simple but useful. I'll configure H2 file DB by default and add a comment for Postgres. Actually let me add a `application-postgres.properties` profile too, and Postgres driver dependency. Hmm, that adds complexity. I'll keep H2 runtime + include PostgreSQL runtime driver commented? Never add commented dependencies ideally.

I think best: H2 file-based default, PostgreSQL driver included as runtime (so it's ready) and commented properties for switching. Actually including postgres driver but H2 default is fine and common. But simpler is better. Let me include both H2 (runtime) and PostgreSQL (runtime) — but that's extra. The user said "a relational database" generically. I'll go with H2 for zero-config runnable, and document how to switch. Since I can't create docs, I'll put comments in application.properties.

Also `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update` and `open-in-view=false`.

Let me also add a simple test using @DataJpaTest with H2.

Let me write the files. Use Java 21, package com.example.demo.

pom.xml:
- parent spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.3
- properties java.version 21
- dependencies: spring-boot-starter-data-jpa, h2 runtime, spring-boot-starter-test test
- build plugin spring-boot-maven-plugin

Let me create .gitignore for Maven/Java.

Let me also add a CommandLineRunner? A `DataLoader` could demonstrate. I'll add a small `@Component` CommandLineRunner in the app that saves sample data only if empty. Hmm, might be over-engineering. I'll keep the app focused but include a main app class. Maybe skip CommandLineRunner to avoid side effects. Actually a demonstration is helpful and shows it works. I'll include it as a separate `DataInitializer` in config? Let me keep it minimal: app class only + entity + repo + test. That's clean.

Actually, to make the project genuinely useful and demonstrate JPA persistence, I'll include a small service? No. The user just wants setup. Entity + repository is the core of "using JPA/Hibernate repositories".

Let me create the directory structure.
Java and Maven aren't installed in this environment, so I'll scaffold the full project structure by hand (you'll run the Maven commands locally/CI). Latest Spring Boot release is `3.5.3`.

Let me verify there's no compile issue by checking Java syntax... no Java compiler available. I can at least reason it through. `@Query("select c from Customer c where c.email like %:domain")` — this is invalid JPQL. The `%` needs to be concatenated: `like concat('%', :domain)` or `like %:domain` is actually invalid syntax. Let me fix that to use a proper query. Use `like concat('%', :domain)`. Good catch.

Also the entity `@Column(name="created_at", nullable=false, updatable=false)` with default Instant.now() — fine.

Java/Maven aren't installed here, so I couldn't compile. Once you have JDK 21 + Maven, verify with:

```
mvn test        # runs the @DataJpaTest repository tests
mvn spring-boot:run
```

Notes:
- Default datasource is a file-based H2 DB under `./data`, so records survive restarts (`ddl-auto=update`); H2 console at `/h2-console`.
- PostgreSQL driver is already on the classpath — run with `--spring.profiles.active=postgres` to use it.
